what: MP Materials mines and processes rare earth elements at Mountain Pass in California, the only operating rare earth mine in the United States. It is building the capability to turn that ore into separated oxides, then into metal and finally into the permanent magnets used in electric motors.
customers: Magnet manufacturers, and increasingly automotive and defence customers directly. It has agreements with the US government and with large manufacturers to supply magnets made domestically.
money: Ore concentrate and separated rare earth oxides, principally neodymium-praseodymium.
Metal, alloy and finished permanent magnets from its Texas facility, ramping up.
moat: Mountain Pass is strategically unique: China controls the great majority of global rare earth processing, and Western governments and manufacturers want supply that does not depend on it. That gives MP something closer to a policy-backed position than an ordinary mining asset, including price floors and offtake commitments from the US government.
risks: Free cash flow was about negative $537.3M in the trailing period as the magnet and separation facilities are built. The business consumes cash well before it generates it.
Revenue has fallen from $527.5M in 2022 to about $224.4M in 2025, because rare earth prices collapsed from their peak.
The shares trade at about 16.3 times sales and 132 times EV/EBITDA while the company is loss-making, which assumes the magnet business succeeds at scale.
China can influence rare earth prices directly through export policy and production quotas, and has done so.
Building magnet manufacturing from scratch is a hard industrial problem that Western firms have repeatedly struggled with.
opportunities: Cash of about $1.8B against $1.0B of debt gives an unusually strong position for a development-stage industrial business.
Government support, including price floors and purchase commitments, substantially reduces the commodity risk that normally dominates mining.
Moving downstream from ore to finished magnets multiplies the revenue per tonne many times over.
Sixteen analysts average a $65.94 target against a $36.53 price, reflecting the value placed on the magnet business once running.
watch: Magnet production volumes and shipments. The mining is proved; the entire investment case rests on whether MP can manufacture magnets at commercial scale and quality, and output is the only honest measure.
